skeptics.explanation: BPTT_fixed_win is NOT a clean recurrent-credit ceiling: it trains {W_rec, b, W_out} with AdamW (train_bptt lines 304-310), while the numerator arms (fixed_reservoir, plastic_eprop, dualtc) train W_out by a one-step delta rule and never train the bias b (train_eprop lines 180, 199-204). So the denominator differs from the numerator arms in THREE ways, not one: recurrent-credit rule [intended], W_out optimizer (AdamW vs delta), and trained-bias (AdamW b vs frozen b=0). Proof it is read-out-dominated: at a block boundary h_0=0 (reset), so at within-block position 1 rec=h_0@W_rec.t()=0 and h_1=alpha*tanh(W_in x_1 + b) (rnn_forward_step lines 91-94) — W_rec has provably ZERO effect on bucket-1, so any bucket-1 gap is pure read-out. From the JSON: fixed_reservoir bucket-1 = -3.3008, BPTT_fixed_win bucket-1 = -1.5103 => read-out-only gain +1.7905, while dualtc bucket-1 = -3.3085 (denied that boost). Critically, that read-out-only +1.79 EXCEEDS the entire deep denominator gain bptt_deep_gain = -1.4006-(-2.7599) = +1.3593. BPTT_fixed_win's near-flat bucket profile (-1.51..-1.40) and its shallow gain (+1.88) > deep gain (+1.36) confirm the denominator is a depth-independent read-out boost, not depth-specific recurrent credit; its true recurrent-credit content is ~0-or-negative. Hence '81% of full-BPTT recurrent-credit margin' is mislabeled and not robust to a fair matched read-out. Direction: the read-out confound makes 81% CONSERVATIVE (a matched read-out would raise it), and the load-bearing deep-specific dualtc lift (+0.497 over plain at ctx17-127, shallow flat, shuffle collapses to -2.79) is measured within matched delta-read-out arms and is untouched — so the qualitative claim survives; only the precise fraction framing is invalid. Under-training is a secondary opposite-direction concern (BPTT_fixed_win agg-CE 5.68 vs same_net 3.40 reflects the frozen-W_in capacity floor, not obvious non-convergence).
skeptics.recommended_control: Rerun a MATCHED-read-out denominator, 'BPTT_matched_readout': same train_bptt but FREEZE b (=0) and replace the AdamW W_out update with the SAME one-step delta rule the e-prop arms use (or, symmetrically, give the e-prop/dualtc arms an AdamW W_out+b read-out) — so the ONLY arm difference is the W_rec credit rule. Recompute frac_clean_deep against that denominator; the fraction 'of recurrent credit' is only valid there. Also report per-arm bucket-1 margins as a read-out-only diagnostic (they must be ~equal under a fair comparison; currently they differ by +1.79), and log the BPTT_fixed_win train-CE trajectory to confirm convergence (rule out the opposite, under-training, direction). Do NOT commit '81% of recurrent-credit margin' until the matched-read-out denominator is in hand.

skeptics.explanation:
VERIFIED NUMBERS (r2b json + runner): fixed floor deep -2.7599; plain e-prop deep -2.1581 (clean frac (−2.1581+2.7599)/(−1.4006+2.7599)=0.4427=44%); dualtc deep -1.6613 (frac 1.0986/1.3593=0.808=81%); BPTT_fixed_win ceiling -1.4006. Shuffle collapses to -2.790 (below floor). All confirmed.

CONFOUND (real, but acknowledged-pending in the doc, not hidden): (1) NO a_slow sweep exists — only two dualtc jsons, both a_slow=0.01. (2) The CLI default is a_slow=0.02 (line 664, ~50-tok horizon) but the run OVERRODE it to 0.01 (json line 37) — a value WAS chosen, so the 'a-priori, principled' framing is at least partly a selection. (3) The decisive theoretical issue the shuffle control does NOT address: a_slow is ENTANGLED with the effective W_rec learning rate. e_slow is a leaky integrator with INPUT GAIN 1 (line 214: e_slow=(1-a_slow)*e_slow+incr), so its steady-state magnitude ∝ 1/a_slow. At a_slow=0.01, e_slow's SS magnitude (~100·incr) is ~30× e_fast's (~incr/alpha=3.3·incr, line 213). Since credit=e_fast+e_slow (line 225) and lr_rec is fixed at 0.001 for BOTH arms, the dualtc arm's effective recurrent LR is ~30× the plain arm's — and it scales as ~alpha/a_slow as you vary a_slow. So the a_slow axis is simultaneously a horizon axis AND an lr_rec axis.

THEORY OF THE LANDSCAPE / IS 0.01 A PEAK: too-fast (a_slow≳0.05, τ≲20): e_slow≈e_fast, collapses toward plain 44%. Matched (a_slow~0.008-0.03, τ~33-125): spans the deep bucket 17-127, near-peak. Too-slow (a_slow≲0.005, τ>block=128, and e_slow is reset per block, line 195): TWO degrading effects — (a) over-integration smears which past step is credited (partial loss of the very structure the shuffle proves is load-bearing), (b) magnitude/lr blows up ∝1/a_slow at fixed lr_rec → likely W_rec instability. So the landscape is plausibly a genuine PEAK (declining on BOTH sides), not a left-plateau — meaning a much-worse a_slow does exist and 0.01 could sit at/near that peak partly for lr-magnitude reasons, not purely horizon-match. This is exactly the silent-cherry-pick risk: 0.01 vs the 0.02 default may have been favored because 0.02 under-integrates/under-updates.

WHY IT DOES NOT INVALIDATE: the claim is a CAPABILITY/existence claim ('biological one-step-local credit CAN reach ~81%'). A slow-eligibility timescale is a legitimate a-priori hyperparameter (like alpha); reaching 81% at a principled value (matched to the measured deep bucket) with a PASSING structural shuffle control is a valid demonstration that the capability exists. The doc honestly scopes it (line 5/27: 'single a_slow (0.01)... a_slow robustness sweep pending') and does NOT overclaim robustness. The qualitative claim (dual-timescale eligibility substantially lifts deep credit over 44%) is theoretically robust across a broad band and will survive. What must change is the HEADLINE PRECISION: '~81%' is likely a near-optimal-a_slow (upper-shoulder/peak) number, not a band-representative one, and the horizon-vs-lr attribution is unproven.

PREDICTION: qualitative lift ROBUST (dualtc >> plain 44% for all a_slow in ~[0.008,0.03]); the specific 81% is a mild PEAK — expect ~65-75% at a_slow=0.02, ~81% at 0.01, and a DROP (not plateau) at a_slow≤0.005 driven by the magnitude/lr coupling. After a magnitude-controlled sweep the honest headline becomes '~70-81% across a_slow∈[0.008,0.02]'.
skeptics.recommended_control: Run a GEOMETRIC a_slow sweep a_slow∈{0.002,0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1} (τ≈{500,200,100,50,20,10}), spanning sub-block to super-block horizons, folded into the 6-seed replication (≥2 seeds/point minimum). Report frac_clean_deep(a_slow). CRITICAL — disentangle horizon from update-magnitude, otherwise the sweep just re-discovers an lr sweet-spot: add a magnitude-CONTROLLED variant by converting e_slow to a true EMA with input gain a_slow (e_slow=(1-a_slow)*e_slow + a_slow*incr) so its steady-state magnitude is a_slow-INVARIANT; re-sweep and compare curves. Prediction to test: the raw (gain-1) curve peaks sharply near 0.01 (magnitude-coupled), while the EMA-normalized curve is a broad flat plateau that peaks at a DIFFERENT/lower a_slow (pure-horizon) — if 81% only appears with the gain-1 form at 0.01, the number is partly an lr artifact and must be reported as such. Secondary fairness control (addresses the same coupling on the plain baseline): re-run plain e-prop with lr_rec scaled ~alpha/a_slow (~30×) to confirm plain's 44% is not merely lr-under-tuned. GATE: claim '81%' as validated only if the number holds within ±~8pts across a_slow∈[0.008,0.02] AND survives at 6 seeds AND the EMA-normalized sweep still shows a large lift over plain; otherwise soften the headline to the band the sweep supports.

skeptics.explanation:
The dualtc-SHUFFLE (train_eprop lines 224-231: e_use=e+e_slow, flattened over n*n, torch.randperm(n*n), then dW=lr_rec*(L.unsqueeze(2)*e_use).mean(0)) is a VALID and decisive control for the sub-confound it targets, but does NOT formally instantiate the full magnitude family, so it is necessary-but-not-provably-complete.

(1) MAGNITUDE preservation: the permutation preserves the eligibility MULTISET exactly -> sum|e_use| and sum(e_use^2) identical (L1/L2 of the eligibility preserved). It does NOT exactly preserve ||dW||, because the permute crosses the j-axis (full n*n, not per-row), so values are reweighted by a different L_j. This is minor. Crucially, the shuffle arm still carries the FULL ~2x combined eligibility magnitude (e+e_slow) yet lands at deep -2.790, BELOW plain (-2.158) AND below the frozen fixed_reservoir floor (-2.760). So 'doubled eligibility magnitude with broken structure buys nothing (in fact hurts)' is demonstrated directly -> the eligibility-magnitude confound IS controlled.

(2) STRUCTURE: fully broken. The full n*n permute destroys the j-i alignment L_j*e[j,i] (moves mass across both pre- and post-synaptic axes). Confirmed.

(3) The SUBTLER confound the skeptic raises -- plain e-prop at 2x lr_rec (matching dualtc's ~2x update magnitude WITHOUT the slow horizon) -- is genuinely NOT instantiated by the shuffle. The shuffle controls the ELIGIBILITY-MAGNITUDE sub-confound but not the STEP-SIZE sub-confound. However this missing control is analytically null on the DEEP bucket: with alpha=0.3 (args), fast eligibility decays as (1-alpha)^lag = 0.7^lag -> 2.3e-3 at lag 17, ~1e-17 at lag 110. Scaling lr_rec multiplies a ~zero fast trace, so plain-2x-lr cannot manufacture deep credit; only the slow trace (0.99^lag = 0.84 at lag17, 0.33 at lag110) carries deep-lag mass. Empirically this is corroborated by deep-SPECIFICITY: shallow plain -3.2810 vs dualtc -3.2821 (identical to 3dp; lift 0.001), deep +0.497. A step-size/magnitude effect would amplify where eligibility is LARGEST = SHALLOW, i.e. the OPPOSITE of the observed deep-only lift. So the plain-2x-lr control is very likely null and its absence does not overturn the ~81% claim.

NET: the shuffle validly refutes 'the lift is eligibility magnitude/capacity' (doubled-magnitude+broken-structure collapses below the floor) and the credit-STRUCTURE story stands. The one honest gap is that the step-size sub-confound is not empirically instantiated -- it is closed only by analysis (alpha=0.3 decay math) + the deep-specificity signature, not by a run.
skeptics.recommended_control: Add ONE cheap arm: plain e-prop (fast eligibility only) at 2x lr_rec (0.002), and ideally a second at lr_rec scaled to match dualtc's mean |e_use| (effective step-size match). Expected/required outcome to fully close the magnitude confound: DEEP margin stays ~ plain (-2.16, NO lift toward BPTT_fixed_win) and any change appears in SHALLOW, confirming the deep lift is the slow-trace HORIZON, not step size. This is belt-and-suspenders: the shuffle + deep-specificity + alpha=0.3 decay math already make it very likely null, but running it removes the last analytic-only assumption. Fold it into the running 6-seed replication so it is a per-seed control, not a single point.

skeptics.explanation: The ~81% headline (dualtc closes 81% of BPTT_fixed_win's deep recurrent-credit gain over the echo-state floor: gain 1.0986/1.3593=0.8082, r2b json) is arithmetically correct, passes the dualtc-shuffle anti-cheat (deep -1.661 -> -2.790, below plain and below floor), is grad-checked, and uses the correct frozen-W_in denominator. It is NOT overturned by this lens. The CONFOUND is in the finding's interpretation of the residual. R2b finding line 26 asserts verbatim "The residual ~19% is the genuinely off-diagonal cross-unit gradient (SnAp-2 / multi-layer territory)." That attribution is unsupported by the data. Mechanistically, dualtc's eligibility is PROVABLY PURELY DIAGONAL: runner lines 211-214 give both e_fast and e_slow the same own-unit increment incr=psi*h_prev with scalar decays (1-alpha) and (1-a_slow); W_rec never enters the eligibility recursion, so the two timescales add ZERO off-diagonal (cross-unit) credit -- they only lengthen the horizon of the RTRL-diagonal sensitivity. Therefore the experiment establishes only an UPPER BOUND: off-diagonal <= 19%. The remaining 0.2607-margin gap is the SUM of (a) genuinely off-diagonal cross-unit gradient, (b) residual HORIZON mis-fit -- a single a_slow=0.01 exponential is a poor basis for the full within-block pos-17..127 horizon spread; a slower a_slow or a SPREAD of slow diagonal timescales (still no forward change, still purely diagonal) could climb past 81% toward a higher diagonal-reachable ceiling, and (c) OPTIMIZER asymmetry (e-prop fixed lr_rec=0.001 SGD-style vs BPTT AdamW+grad-clip -- part of the gap survives identical gradients). No horizon-saturation control isolates (a) from (b)+(c). The a_slow sweep is listed as pending only to test robustness of the 81%, not whether more diagonal timescale closes the residual; and the one spread-of-timescales arm (ALIF, rho log-uniform [30,300]) was NEGATIVE for an unrelated forward-state reason (-beta*a degraded the tanh representation), so it does not cleanly test spread-of-eligibility-without-forward-change. Reconciliation of the paradox: a diagonal rule reaches 81% because on this leaky-tanh reservoir (spectral 1.1) BPTT_fixed_win's deep advantage over the floor is MOSTLY long-horizon own-unit diagonal credit, with cross-unit recurrent-Jacobian corrections being second-order (<=19%). So the frontier is plausibly "nearly closed by horizon," not "off-diagonal-bound." Severity moderate (not minor): the mislabel is load-bearing for the research narrative -- R1 line 42 already earmarks expensive SnAp-2 / multi-layer / future-error-predictor mechanisms as the diagnosed-cause next rung, which the off-diagonal framing would justify, when a cheap purely-diagonal lever may capture much of the residual. This is exactly the project's own "disguised boundary" failure mode (a surpassable horizon-limit relabeled as a fundamental wall). Not fatal because the 81% number and the "biological one-step-local diagonal credit reaches ~81% of the recurrent-credit-rule-only deep margin" claim remain valid; if anything a horizon residual STRENGTHENS the biological-credit thesis (diagonal could reach even more).
skeptics.recommended_control: Add two controls before labeling the residual off-diagonal. (1) a_slow SWEEP + MULTI-TIMESCALE eligibility arm: run a_slow in {0.02,0.01,0.005,0.003} and a summed multi-trace variant (several e_slow at different a_slow, still purely diagonal, no forward change). If frac_clean_deep SATURATES below 1.0 across the sweep -> residual is genuinely off-diagonal (label justified); if it keeps CLIMBING -> residual is horizon and the off-diagonal label is wrong. (2) DECISIVE: a DIAGONAL-BPTT ceiling arm -- full backprop over W_rec but with the off-diagonal recurrent Jacobian DETACHED (differentiate only the diagonal (1-alpha) path, e.g. h.detach() on the cross-unit rec term). If diagonal-BPTT deep ~= full BPTT_fixed_win deep, then off-diagonal contributes ~0 and the entire 19% is horizon+optimizer (label refuted); the gap between diagonal-BPTT and dualtc is then the pure horizon+optimizer residual. Also match the optimizer (train dualtc's W_rec with Adam, or a diagonal-BPTT with the same lr schedule) to remove optimizer asymmetry from the attributed residual. Reframe the finding to state "off-diagonal <= 19% (upper bound); the genuinely off-diagonal part is untested pending a horizon-saturation / diagonal-BPTT control" rather than "residual = off-diagonal."

skeptics.explanation:
LEAKAGE (does NOT invalidate). The eval is an internal contiguous 90/10 split of tinystories_train.txt (line 692-697); vocab (build_vocab, line 693) and the add-1 bigram P_bi (line 707) are both fit on TRAIN ONLY, so there is no fitted-object leakage. TinyStories is heavily templated/near-duplicated, so an eval story likely has a near-twin in train, but this cannot inflate the 81% because: (a) the model is a 300-unit fixed-random-W_in leaky-tanh reservoir with a linear delta-rule read-out — negligible capacity to memorize ~1000 held-out stories; (b) the margin is bigram_CE - model_CE, and the bigram (fit on the same templated train) absorbs the shared local repetition; (c) decisively, 81% is a FRACTION (dualtc-gain-over-fixed / BPTT_fixed_win-gain-over-fixed) with the SAME frozen W_in, same eval, same bucket for numerator and denominator — any shared near-duplication benefit cancels. So leakage refines absolute-margin interpretation at most, not the fraction.

DEEP-SPECIFICITY (the real gap, moderate). The whole scientific value is the word "long-range" (100+ token) — the pre-registered expectation was e-prop reaches only SHALLOW, so "deep" being genuinely far is load-bearing. But the runner lumps positions 17-127 into ONE pooled by_bucket entry (summarize, line 413/420); there is NO resolution to distinguish mid-range (~ctx32) saturation from true 100+-token credit. I CANNOT confirm from the artifacts whether the +0.497 dualtc-over-plain deep gain is spread to ctx>96 or concentrated at ctx17-40. Partial reassurance from arithmetic: eval counts are equal per position (lines 359-360), so the pooled deep margin equal-weights all 111 positions; a +0.497 pooled gain concentrated only in positions 17-32 (16 of 111) would require ~+3.45 nats/position there, which would flip those positions strongly positive (implausible for a reservoir negative everywhere else) — so the gain provably CANNOT be ctx32-only; it must extend well past ctx48. And a_slow=0.01 gives a genuine ~100-token eligibility horizon, reset only at the 128 boundary. So the gain is distributed, not a mid-range artifact — but the deepest sub-range (97-127) is still unverified directly.

SHALLOW-UNCHANGED/DEEP-IMPROVED split is mechanistically coherent, not a metric artifact: e_slow accumulates over p tokens, so it is ~zero at shallow p (shallow ~unchanged) and large at deep p; and the dualtc_shuffle control (permute the combined eligibility, magnitude kept) collapses deep -1.66 -> -2.79 (below fixed floor -2.76), so the deep lift is credit-STRUCTURE not magnitude/capacity. The bigram is position-independent, so the observed deep improvement reflects the reservoir actually using accumulated within-block context.

SCOPE CAVEAT on the running 6-seed replication: the stream (words[:2M]) and the 90/10 split are DATA-DETERMINISTIC; the seed only varies init RNG + torch/np seed. So the 6-seed run tests init-variance ONLY and will NOT catch any corpus/near-duplication/deep-bucketing confound — those are frozen across all 6 seeds. Do not present 6-seed agreement as evidence against the leakage/deep-specificity confounds.
skeptics.recommended_control: Before committing, add a per-position (or finer sub-bucket) breakdown of the DEEP range and confirm the effect is sustained at the far end, not ctx32-saturated: split 17-127 into e.g. 17-32 / 33-64 / 65-96 / 97-127 in summarize(), and verify (i) dualtc's gain over fixed_reservoir and (ii) frac_clean_deep vs BPTT_fixed_win are both still substantial in the deepest 97-127 sub-bucket for seed 42. Cheap (re-eval only, no retrain, from saved arms or one rerun). Second, run the runner's existing --permute-stream once with the dualtc arm: with sequential structure destroyed and the bigram refit, the dualtc deep gain over fixed should collapse to ~0 — the direct test that the deep margin reflects real long-range language structure, not a within-block position artifact (currently only covered indirectly by the fixed/shuffle nulls). Third, in the writeup, either report the far-sub-bucket number as the load-bearing 'long-range' evidence or soften 'long-range/100+-token' to 'deep within-block (>=17-token, distributed to ctx>~64)'. None of these is expected to overturn the ~81%; they convert the deep LABEL from arithmetic-inferred to directly-verified.

skeptics.explanation:
I read train_eprop end-to-end, the two JSONs, and the R2b finding. The mechanics are sound; the exposure is FRAMING of the denominator, not a computational cheat.

CLEAN (no confound):
- Slow eligibility resets per block, symmetric with the fast trace. In train_eprop the block loop `for j in range(nb)` (L190) allocates BOTH `e = zeros(n,n)` (L194) and `e_slow = zeros(n,n) if dualtc` (L195) fresh each block. No cross-block leak; a_slow=0.01 (~100-tok horizon) lives entirely within the 128-block.
- No cross-arm leakage via shared init. `init=build_init(...)` (L717) is built once; every arm re-copies via torch.tensor(init[...]) (train_eprop L178-182), so each starts from an identical fresh copy. The only shared mutable global (torch RNG) only feeds randperm in the shuffle arms — it never touches dualtc.
- fixed_reservoir IS a fair zero-recurrent-CREDIT floor: W_rec frozen (no recurrent learning) but W_out trained by the identical delta rule (L204) and full random-reservoir dynamics active. Both the numerator (dualtc gain) and denominator (BPTT gain) subtract the same floor, so read-out learning + reservoir memory are controlled for. The dualtc-shuffle anti-cheat (keeps update magnitude, permutes structure → collapses to -2.790, below plain AND floor) genuinely rules out a magnitude/capacity artifact, and the deep-SPECIFIC lift (+0.497 at ctx17-127, shallow unchanged) is the correct horizon-extension signature, not a uniform fit improvement. Arithmetic reproduces exactly: (-1.6613-(-2.7599))/(-1.4006-(-2.7599))=1.0986/1.3593=0.8082.

THE CONFOUND (denominator choice / headline scope):
The 81% denominator is BPTT_fixed_win (deep -1.401), the W_in-FROZEN ceiling deliberately handicapped to isolate the recurrent-credit rule. The SAME run contains the actual full-backprop ceiling BPTT_same_net (deep +0.902, agg_ce 3.40 vs dualtc 6.14). Measured against it, the gain-over-floor fraction is 1.099/(0.902-(-2.760))=1.099/3.662 = ~0.30 (~30%), and dualtc's ABSOLUTE deep margin (-1.661) is still WORSE than the add-1 bigram — the model does not beat a bigram at long range in absolute terms; the entire 81% lives in the sub-bigram region between a bad frozen reservoir (-2.76) and a still-sub-bigram frozen-embedding BPTT (-1.40). The claim's WORDING ('~81% of full-BPTT's deep RECURRENT-CREDIT margin', 'on identical frozen embeddings') is technically correct and internally scoped, so it does not overturn. But 'reaches ~81% of full-BPTT' is highly misleadable: a casual reader hears 'e-prop nearly matches backprop,' when against unconstrained full backprop it's ~30% and the missing ~70% is dominated by embedding learning the reservoir setup structurally forbids. The finding's residual-'~19% is the off-diagonal cross-unit gradient' sentence compounds this — 19% is 19% of the frozen-W_in ceiling, not of full backprop.

Secondary (would refine downward, not overturn): bptt_steps=4000 in the JSON (the docstring/claim text says 8000) — if the frozen-W_in denominator is under-converged, its +1.359 gain is understated and 81% is an upper bound; and a_slow=0.01 overrides the 0.02 default (the R2b finding itself lists the a_slow robustness sweep as still-pending, so 0.01 is not yet shown to be non-favorable).

Net: the precisely-worded, frozen-embedding-scoped claim survives; the natural/headline reading is materially weaker (~30% of full BPTT, absolute still sub-bigram). Moderate, refine-not-overturn.
skeptics.recommended_control: In any committed claim, foreground BOTH fractions side by side — ~81% vs BPTT_fixed_win (frozen-embedding recurrent-credit rule) AND ~30% vs BPTT_same_net (unconstrained full backprop) — and state explicitly that dualtc's absolute deep margin (-1.661) is still below the add-1 bigram, i.e. the 81% is 'of the recurrent-credit-rule gap on frozen embeddings,' not 'of full backprop.' The runner already records clean_recurrent_credit_fraction for BPTT_same_net; report it. Additionally: (1) train BPTT_fixed_win to a verified plateau (>4000 steps, show the train-CE flattened) so the denominator is a true ceiling and 81% is not an under-convergence upper bound; (2) run the pending a_slow sweep (0.005-0.05) to confirm 0.01 is not cherry-picked; (3) keep the 6-seed replication at the pre-committed a_slow=0.01 (already running) as the actual validation of significance.

fatal_or_moderate_confounds: MODERATE — bptt-ceiling read-out asymmetry (VERIFIED in code): the 81% denominator (train_bptt fix_win) trains {W_rec, b, W_out} with AdamW, but the numerator arms (fixed_reservoir, plain, dualtc) train only W_out by a one-step delta rule and keep bias b frozen at 0. So the fraction differs from the numerator arms in THREE ways (recurrent-credit rule [intended] + W_out optimizer + trained bias), not one. Proof it is read-out-contaminated: at within-block pos-1 h0=0 so W_rec has ZERO effect, yet fixed_reservoir bucket-1 (-3.30) vs BPTT_fixed_win bucket-1 (-1.51) = +1.79 pure read-out gain, which EXCEEDS the entire deep denominator gain (+1.36). So the denominator's 'recurrent credit' is partly a depth-independent read-out boost. Direction: makes 81% CONSERVATIVE (a fair matched read-out would raise it), so it does not overturn the qualitative claim; but '81% of recurrent-credit margin' is mislabeled until a matched read-out is used.

MODERATE — a_slow entangled with effective recurrent LR (VERIFIED): line 214 gives e_slow input gain 1 (not a_slow), so its steady-state magnitude is proportional to 1/a_slow; at a_slow=0.01 the dualtc effective lr_rec is ~30x plain's at the same nominal lr_rec=0.001. The a_slow axis is simultaneously a horizon axis and an lr axis. a_slow=0.01 also overrode the 0.02 CLI default, so a value was selected. The dualtc-shuffle does NOT control this (it preserves eligibility magnitude but not step size). Undecided: whether the 81% peak is horizon-match or partly an lr-magnitude sweet-spot.

MODERATE — headline scope (full-BPTT vs frozen-embedding, VERIFIED): 81% is the fraction of BPTT_fixed_win's (frozen-W_in) deep recurrent-credit gain over the echo-state floor. Against the unconstrained full-backprop ceiling BPTT_same_net in the SAME run, the fraction is ~30%, and dualtc's ABSOLUTE deep margin (-1.661) is still WORSE than the add-1 bigram. 'reaches ~81% of full-BPTT' reads as 'e-prop nearly matches backprop' when the precise claim is only 'of the recurrent-credit-rule gap on frozen embeddings.'

MODERATE — off-diagonal residual mislabeled: dualtc eligibility is provably PURELY DIAGONAL (own-unit increment, scalar decays, W_rec never enters the recursion), so the finding's assertion 'the residual ~19% is the genuinely off-diagonal cross-unit gradient' is an unsupported UPPER BOUND, not a measurement. The residual is a sum of off-diagonal + horizon-misfit + optimizer asymmetry. Risk: this relabel would justify expensive SnAp-2/multi-layer next rungs when a cheap purely-diagonal multi-timescale lever may capture much of it (the project's own 'disguised boundary' failure mode).

MODERATE — deep-specificity label under-resolved: positions 17-127 are pooled into one bucket, so the load-bearing word 'long-range/100+-token' is arithmetic-inferred, not directly verified at the far end (97-127). Arithmetic bounds the gain away from ctx32-only, but the deepest sub-range is unconfirmed. Also: the running 6-seed replication only varies init RNG — the stream, 90/10 split and bigram are data-deterministic and FROZEN across all 6 seeds, so 6-seed agreement will NOT catch the corpus/deep-bucket/a_slow confounds and must not be presented as doing so.

MINOR — shuffle controls eligibility-magnitude but not step-size: the dualtc-shuffle refutes the capacity/magnitude story (doubled magnitude + broken structure collapses below the floor), but a plain-e-prop-at-matched-step-size arm is not instantiated; it is closed only by the alpha=0.3 fast-decay math (0.7^17=2.3e-3) plus the deep-specific signature.
